messages.text: wait, am i supposed to be sleeping? just realized we haven't formally locked in the db choice yet.
we did. postgres + pgvector. chris argued for it yesterday and i'm not changing it now
right, one datastore. recursive ctes are enough for the graph traversal, no need for neo4j overhead. jane was worried about viz but me and the team agree sql is fine
exactly. i don't want to manage two infra stacks during a hackathon. keep it simple. can you sketch the schema for me? i want to see how you're modeling the relations

sure. actor(id, name, email)
concept(id, label, vector)
actor_concept(actor_id, concept_id, weight)
concept_relation(parent_id, child_id, type)
looks okay. but are you sure about the weight in actor_concept? i thought we just had a boolean presence initially?
i added weight for future flexibility, maybe confidence score from the resolution pipeline? or just set it to 1.0 for now
fine, default 1.0. the idf scoring will happen in the query layer anyway. just make sure the vector column is using the correct dimension (768)
yep, pgvector extension handles that. create type embedding(768). done
good. and the concept_relation table? is that for the hierarchy? like 'machine learning' -> 'deep learning'?
yep. parent/child links. recursive cte can walk up or down from there. should be fast enough
perfect. i'll start writing the resolution logic against this schema tonight. ping me if you change anything in the columns
won't touch it until i hear from you. heading to bed for real now, night john
night. good luck with the dockerfile tomorrow
thanks. hope the gx10 doesn't overheat while you're testing embeddings
it's a desktop, it has fans. sleep well
